handoff_record.entry_point: Task: validate Mass and actor-resident rendered LOD transitions in a live scene (LOD-001 next action from docs/active-threads.md).
work_completed: Added five NLT.VisualLOD.LiveScene.* automation tests driving the two real LOD integration points inside an actual UWorld: a real APlayerController viewer, a real AAvatarCharacter, real Mass entities, and the real HISM instance set.

Covered actor-resident LOD0->LOD1->LOD2->LOD3 and back, hysteresis hold/advance/oscillation, Mesh vs FallbackMesh representation at an identical distance and level, hidden transitions and restoration, viewer fallback with and without a player controller, and Mass HISM instance filtering with per-instance LOD stamping.

Fixed three defects the live tests exposed: BeginPlay never dispatched in a hand-built world (UWorld::BeginPlay reaches actors only via GameMode->StartPlay -> GameState::HandleBeginPlay -> WorldSettings::NotifyBeginPlay), leaving the visualizer's FMassEntityQuery uninitialized so the first Tick hard-asserted and killed the editor; the visualizer's own default LOD policy (Far=8000) kept a 7000cm resident visible as LOD2; and a bare APlayerController does not report the TransformComponent offset it is given.
Drove protected UpdateVisualLOD through the public Actor Tick rather than widening production API for test access.

Corrected README claims that overstated LOD maturity: 'LOD 0-3 population management' for UNLTPopulationScaler, the 'Population LOD scaler' tree label, and 'LOD transition logic for avatar actors' listed as remaining work.
Rewrote the LOD-001 entry in docs/active-threads.md to state what the live tests prove (policy core correct and simulation-isolated) and what they do not (the visual result).
Recorded the four verified integration limitations identified by the Hermes QA review.
work_in_progress: The visual LOD integration remains a proof of concept; the four limitations below are recorded, not fixed.
verified_limitations: Mass LOD levels are decorative: ANLTAgentVisualizer stamps the level into HISM custom data slot 0, but M_SimBody_Base is a MaterialInstanceConstant with HasPerInstanceCustomData=False parented to FBXLegacyPhongSurf, so nothing consumes the value.

The HISM path discards its own benefit every frame: UpdateVisuals calls ClearInstances() and re-adds every instance each tick, with no cluster-tree tuning (BuildTreeAsync, NumClusters, SetTreeHeuristicScale) configured.
Per-agent state map grows unbounded: AgentVisualLevels only ever Adds and is never pruned when an agent leaves the query.
UNLTPopulationScaler is a stub: ScalePopulation only logs and assigns AgentCount, drives nothing, and has no callers anywhere in the module.
blockers: The installed UE 5.8 distribution reports that server targets are not currently supported, so WorldEngineServer cannot be compiled on this machine.
Live-scene tests run with -nullrhi, so they validate state transitions and simulation isolation, not rendered pixels. Visual confirmation remains open.
decisions_made: Treat the Hermes characterisation as correct, but verify each claim against the source before accepting it; all five were confirmed with evidence.

Do not silently fix the integration limitations: material authoring is OpenCode/graphics lane, and implementing or retiring UNLTPopulationScaler is an architecture decision reserved to the Human Principal.
Position residents relative to the measured viewer location instead of moving the viewer, so asserted distances are exact regardless of how a bare PlayerController resolves its view target.
escalations: Human Principal: decide whether UNLTPopulationScaler should be implemented or removed; the README previously advertised it as working LOD 0-3 population management.
OpenCode/graphics lane: wire a material to read the per-instance LOD custom data, adopt incremental HISM updates instead of clear-and-rebuild, and prune AgentVisualLevels for departed agents.
